22-070.r: Lok Sabha/Assembly polls use First Past the Post: most votes wins, 50 percent not needed; Speaker to majority and Deputy Speaker to Opposition is only tradition, not in Constitution (Art 93).
hi: First Past the Post (सर्वाधिक मत से जीत प्रणाली)

22-071.r: Lok Sabha Speaker → 'chosen' by the House from among its members (Art 93), along with the Deputy Speaker.
22-071.t: The Constitution's word is 'chosen', not 'elected', 'nominated' or 'appointed'.

22-072.r: Lok Sabha Speaker → chosen by all the members of the Lok Sabha (not by all MPs, not by the public, not by majority party alone).

22-073.r: Speaker takes no oath of office; oaths: President by Chief Justice of India; Vice-President, PM and Council of Ministers by the President.

22-074.r: Speaker and Deputy Speaker take no oath of office (Arts 93-95); President (Art 60), VP (Art 69), PM and Ministers (Art 75(4)), SC Judges (Art 124(6)) do.

22-075.r: Lok Sabha Speaker resigns by writing addressed to the Deputy Speaker (Article 94).
22-075.t: Not to the President; the Speaker's resignation letter goes to the Deputy Speaker.

22-077.r: Speaker removed by a Lok Sabha resolution passed by a majority of all the then members (Art 94(c)), after at least 14 days' notice.

22-080.r: While his removal resolution is considered (Art 96): Speaker cannot preside, but can speak and take part, and can vote in the first instance (not on a tie).

22-081.r: Speaker keeps office after Lok Sabha dissolution till the new House first meets (Art 94); need not quit his party; removal needs majority of all members and 14 days' notice.

22-082.r: Speaker's resignation → addressed to Deputy Speaker (Art 94(b)); must be a member when elected; not at President's pleasure; does not vacate office on dissolution.

22-083.r: Speaker: chosen by Lok Sabha from its own members; not at President's pleasure; removed by majority of all then members; resignation letter to Deputy Speaker.

22-084.r: Not true: 'may become member within six months' → only a sitting member can be Speaker (Art 93); vacates on ceasing to be member (94(a)); stays after dissolution.

22-085.r: Pro-tem Speaker → administers oath to newly elected members and conducts proceedings till the regular Speaker is chosen.

22-086.r: Pro-tem Speaker → one of the senior-most members of the new Lok Sabha; list goes via Minister of Parliamentary Affairs to the President for approval.

22-087.r: Speaker presides over joint sitting (Art 118(4)); certifies Money Bills (Art 110(4)); votes only on a tie (Art 100(1)); during his removal resolution he can speak (Art 96).

22-088.r: Speaker does not vote in the first instance; he has a casting vote only in case of a tie (Art 100(1)).

22-089.r: Speaker uses his casting vote only in case of a tie (equality of votes), under Article 100(1).

22-091.r: First Lok Sabha Speaker → G.V. Mavalankar (1952-1956); then M. Ananthasayanam Iyengar (1956-1962), Hukum Singh (1962-1967); Om Birla since 2019.

22-092.r: First Speaker of Lok Sabha → G.V. Mavalankar (15 May 1952 till his death, 27 February 1956); called 'Father of the Lok Sabha' by Nehru.

22-094.r: First Speaker to face a no-confidence motion → G.V. Mavalankar; moved by Vigneshwar Missir and J.B. Kripalani, 15 December 1954; rejected 18 December 1954.

22-095.r: First woman Speaker of Lok Sabha → Meira Kumar, chosen unopposed; served June 2009 to June 2014.

22-096.r: First woman Speaker of Lok Sabha → Meira Kumar, Speaker of the 15th Lok Sabha (2009-2014).

22-097.r: Speakers: 11th Lok Sabha → P.A. Sangma; 12th → G.M.C. Balayogi; 14th → Somnath Chatterjee; 17th and 18th → Om Birla.

22-098.r: Deputy Speaker: election date fixed by Speaker (Rule 8(1)); no rule he be from opposition or ruling party; same powers as Speaker when presiding, no appeal (Art 95(1)).

22-099.r: Lok Sabha Deputy Speakers: P.M. Sayeed (1999); Charanjit Singh Atwal (14th); Karia Munda (15th); M. Thambidurai (16th); post vacant since May 2019.

22-100.r: Deputy Speaker presiding over Lok Sabha (Art 95) → can vote only in the event of equality of votes (casting vote).

22-101.r: First tribal Speaker of Lok Sabha → P.A. Sangma, 11th Lok Sabha, from 23 May 1996.

22-102.r: Lok Sabha Secretariat → under direct control of the Speaker; authority exercised through the Secretary (Art 98; rules 124 and 124-A).
22-102.t: Not under Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs or PM; Parliament's secretariats are independent of the executive.

22-104.r: Lok Sabha Secretariat staff → recruitment rules framed by President after consulting Speaker (Art 98(3)); individual appointment orders issued by the Speaker (Rule 6, 1955 Rules).

22-105.r: Women in 17th Lok Sabha → 78 members (over 14%); most from UP and West Bengal (11 each); 106th Amendment Act, 2023 reserves one-third seats for women.
22-105.c: The explanation uses 17th Lok Sabha data. In the 15th Lok Sabha women were just over 10%, Congress had the most, Rajasthan elected three and Uttar Pradesh the most, so (c) fits.

22-106.r: Fewest women in Lok Sabha → 1977 (only 19); most → General Election 2019 (78).

22-107.r: Recognised Opposition party/Leader of Opposition → at least 10% of Lok Sabha (54 of 543); post vacant in 16th and 17th Lok Sabha; Rahul Gandhi in 18th.

22-108.r: First Lok Sabha: Congress 364 of 489 seats, CPI second (16), not Swatantra Party; Leader of Opposition first recognised in 1969; needs 10% (55 seats), not 75.

23-001.r: Rajya Sabha maximum strength → 250 (238 States/UTs + 12 nominated, Art 80); present 245 (225 States, 8 UTs, 12 nominated).

23-002.r: Rajya Sabha → up to 238 members elected for States/UTs plus 12 nominated by President → 'more than one'; permanent body; members serve six years.

23-003.r: Rajya Sabha → maximum 250 members, of which 12 nominated by the President; not more than 238 from States and UTs (Art 80).

23-004.r: States' seats in Rajya Sabha → in ratio of their population (not equal); seats allotted in the Fourth Schedule.

23-005.r: UTs ARE represented in Rajya Sabha (Delhi 3, Puducherry 1, J&K 4); election disputes → judiciary via election petition; Parliament = President + Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha (Art 79).

23-006.r: Rajya Sabha members → elected by elected MLAs of the State Legislative Assembly, by proportional representation through Single Transferable Vote (Art 80(4)).

23-007.r: Rajya Sabha: never dissolved; one-third members retire every second year; member's term 6 years (not five); minimum age 30 (not 25).

23-009.r: Rajya Sabha member's tenure → 6 years; House is permanent (Art 83(1)); one-third retire every second year.

23-010.r: Rajya Sabha → permanent House, cannot be dissolved (Art 83(1)); one-third members retire every two years; each member elected for six years.
23-010.h: Six-two-third: six-year term; every two years, one-third retire.

23-015.r: Rajya Sabha → not subject to dissolution; members elected by elected MLAs (Art 80(4)); Vice-President is ex-officio Chairman; Attorney General can speak in both Houses.
23-015.t: Rajya Sabha does not choose its Chairman from its members; it elects only the Deputy Chairman.

23-018.r: President nominates 12 members to Rajya Sabha (Art 80), from Literature, Science, Art and Social Services.
23-018.h: 12 nominees from 'LSAS': Literature, Science, Art, Social service.

23-020.r: Rajya Sabha candidate: at least 30 years old; no office of profit; need not be a voter of that State (requirement removed, RP Act amendment, 2003).

23-021.r: Minimum age to contest for Rajya Sabha (Council of States) → 30 years.

23-022.r: First actress nominated to Rajya Sabha → Nargis Dutt (1980-1981); Vaijayanthimala (1993-1999); Devika Rani → first Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1969).

23-023.r: Art 249 → Rajya Sabha resolution (two-thirds present and voting) lets Parliament, not Rajya Sabha alone, legislate on a State List subject in national interest; for whole or part of India.

23-027.r: Rajya Sabha: cannot reject/amend Money Bill, only recommend within 14 days, which Lok Sabha may reject (Art 109); cannot vote on Demands for Grants; can discuss Annual Financial Statement.

23-029.r: Money Bill → cannot be introduced in Rajya Sabha; only in Lok Sabha, with the President's prior recommendation.

23-030.r: Money Bill amended by Rajya Sabha → Lok Sabha may accept or reject its recommendations and proceed (Art 109(2)); Rajya Sabha must return it within 14 days.

23-031.r: Lok Sabha exclusive → Money Bill introduction, rejection/amendment (Art 109), Council of Ministers' accountability (Art 75(3)); creating All India Services → Rajya Sabha power (Art 312).

23-032.r: Exclusive Lok Sabha power → no-confidence motion (Art 75(3)); Emergency approval needs both Houses within one month; President's impeachment charge by either House (Art 61(1)).

23-033.r: Rajya Sabha special powers (2/3 present and voting): Art 249 → Parliament may legislate on State List; Art 312 → create All India Services incl. All-India Judicial Service.
